summary: Edge cookie scope clash breaks tenant model pin during canary override
description:
Issue summary: BrightLearn reported intermittent model version switches for a subset of users during our canary rollout. The tenant had explicitly pinned model redwood-llama-compat-v2-13b-q4, but traffic from ~3% of sessions was routed to the canary variant.

Impact: Customer reports degraded responses and an increase in quality errors for training-data ingestion workflows. Observed for ~60 tenants but only BrightLearn reported as it correlates with their traffic pattern. Potential P1 for the customer because pinned model selection was violated during a production rollout.

Environment: prod/us-east (edge-proxy fronting requests, control-plane orchestrator managing rollouts, dedicated pool for BrightLearn).

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Customer issues requests with tenant token and cookie set by their web app domain (app.brightlearn.com).
2) Requests pass through edge-proxy which applies cookie scoping and SSO header rewrite.
3) During canary weight increase for redwood-llama-compat-v2-13b-q4 -> redwood-llama-compat-v2-13b-canary, ~3% of requests from the tenant were routed to the canary despite an explicit tenant pin in the route metadata.

Observed behavior:
- Session affinity appears to break for requests that include a legacy cookie with a domain attribute of ".brightlearn.com" and an updated cookie with path "/app". Edge normalization logic dropped the tenant affinity cookie for certain keep-alive/retry flows, and subsequent routing used weight-based selection without honoring the pin.

Expected behavior: pinned tenant model selection must take precedence over canary weighting for all sessions bearing a valid pin token. Edge cookie normalization must not invalidate affinity cookies used by the routing mesh.

Immediate workaround applied: Support instructed customer to clear the legacy cookie; we temporarily disabled an edge header rewrite rule (edge-proxy v2.13.1) for the BrightLearn routing key which prevented cookie rewriting. This restored pin coherence for affected sessions within ~5 minutes.

investigation_notes: Hypothesis A: Edge cookie normalization rule (introduced in edge-proxy v2.13.1) aggressively drops cookies with overlapping domain/path attributes which removes the tenant affinity marker used by orchestrator.

Hypothesis B: Keep-alive connection retry path triggers a header rehydration codepath that fails to include the pin header when both cookies exist, causing orchestrator to fall back to weight routing.
Trace: request_id=ab12cd34 shows edge logged cookie drop followed by orchestrator decision without pin; control-plane audit shows pin intact for tenant brightlearn at timestamp T-2s.
Reproduction: Simulated session with legacy cookie + new cookie via curl with Cookie header ordering reproduced the drop deterministically in staging when rewrite rule active.

Risk: If edge normalization continues to drop affinity cookies across other tenants with similar cookie rollover patterns, additional customers on dedicated plans might see silent pin violations during future canary ramps.
resolution_notes:
Workaround: disabled the edge header rewrite for BrightLearn routing key and instructed customer to clear legacy cookie. Hotfix: edge-proxy patch prevents affinity cookie drop when a tenant pin header exists; rolled to prod us-east at 2024-11-01 08:45. Next steps: merge orchestrator safeguard so control-plane rejects weight-based routing if pin header is missing but pin metadata present, and add integration test to CI. Customer confirmed behavior restored and quality metrics returned to baseline.

Permanent fix plan: 1) Merge and roll edge-proxy patch (PR #1429) to other regions. 2) Add orchestration-level double-check to consult control-plane pin if header absent but tenant has active explicit pin. 3) Expand canary rollout checklist to include cookie/header rewrite interactions. 4) Postmortem and communication to customers about cookie migration best practices.
